newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: FISCHER WARNS JAPAN AGAINST CRITICISING AUST OVER HANSON
Deputy Prime Minister, Tim Fischer, says Japan can't criticise the Federal Government for its handling of Pauline Hanson and her One Nation Party, because Japan has extreme organisations too.
A senior adviser to Japan's Prime Minister is reported to have criticised the Australian Government's reaction to Hanson's comments.
Foreign minister Alexander Downer has said the comments have been refuted by Japan's ambassador and are completely untrue.

Fischer has told ABC Radio Japan has an organisation with an unreformed view on World War Two. He says Australia has difficulties with that but accepts that Japan is a democracy with freedom of speech.
RALLY IN NEWCASTLE AGAINST BHP CLOSURE
State and Federal politicians will join key union leaders for a public rally in Newcastle today to protest against BHP's decision to close steelmaking in the city.

New South Wales Premier Bob Carr, Federal Opposition Leader Kim Beazley, Federal Shadow Industry Minister Simon Crean and ACTU President Jenny George will be among those addressing the rally at a Park in the Newcastle suburb of Mayfield.
Union organisers will use the rally to further their campaign to keep either BHP or another company making steel in Newcastle.
Kevin Marr from the Australian workers union says they're also trying to put pressure on the Federal Government to develop a new steel industry plan.
STATES HEADING FOR LOSSES
Economic analysts say the improvement in national savings probably won't be as fast as the Federal Government implied in its budget papers.
Access Economics says that's because states are increasing spending, while the Federal Government is reducing its expenses to bring down its deficit.
A report by Access Economics shows the states will be moving from a combined A$2.5 billion surplus this financial year, to a A$337 million deficit next year.
Access Director, Ed Chan, says the states would argue that they're planning to be in balance.
He says the Commonwealth has been trying to get down its big deficits, and squeezing the states' funding.
ALLEGATIONS OF ABUSE AT HOME FOR BOYS
A former teacher at a religious home for boys at Pendle Hill in Sydney's west is calling for an inquiry into alleged mistreatment of children there.
Marion Lee worked as a teacher at the Uniting Protestant Association boys home in the early 1970s.

Lee says children were punished for bet-wetting, the home was cold and much of the time there was no food. She also says she found records at the home showing some of the boys were on high doses of valium.
Now an Education and Ethnic Affairs Consultant, Lee is appealing for former residents to speak out about their treatment as children 20-years ago.
NEW ANTI-SMOKING CAMPAIGN
The Federal Government is launching, today, a new national anti-smoking campaign.
The Government says it adds new urgency to the quit smoking message and sets new precedents for collaboration on a national scale between governments, health proessionals and community organisations.
The Government says depsite past campaigns, cigarette smoking claims over 50 Australian lives a day, and is still the leading preventable cause of premature death in Australia.
MORE FOREST PROTESTERS ARRESTED IN VICTORIA
Thirty protesters have now been arrested at logging blocades in Victoria's East Gippsland region since late last week.
Police arrested six protesters yesterday.
Environmental activists have been moving to the area from Melbourne and Wollongong University, trying to stop logging in the Goolengook area, North East of Orbost.
They are being joined today by Senator Bob Brown.
The area has been subject to the country's first Regional Forest Agreement.
The Wilderness Society's Kate Kennedy says it's clearly the Prime Minister's responsibility to halt logging and review the agreement.
SEARCH CONTINUES FOR CLUES TO WHELAN DISAPPEARANCE
Police will continue searching a large part of the New South Wales Southern Highlands today for clues to the disappearance of Kerry Whelan.
The 39-year old mother of three, vanished from a carpark in Paramatta in Sydney's west more than five-weeks ago.
Several weeks ago police searched a private property at Bungonia, but found nothing.
They're now searching the rugged Morton National Park near Goulburn.
The search is likely to extend to the four-thousand hectare Bungongia State Recreation Area and continue for more than a week.
Police say they're willing to search all caves, tunnels, mines and dams in the area for as long as necessary.
